narrative.summary: Independent verification of sources/chain-ethereum/ (holders.json, payments.json, scan.json) at block 26491756 (0xcf579ca7...7dc4, 2026-11-25T10:59:59Z; next block 11:00:11Z, after T=2026-11-25T11:00:00Z). A full independent replay of every Transfer log of the token (blocks 23501863-26491756) on a public endpoint reproduced the saved scan exactly. No discrepancy was found, so no source or collector file was changed (before/after hashes are identical; see hashes).

fullReplay.method: eth_getLogs(address=token, topics=[Transfer]) in windows of 25 scan chunks (50000 blocks); windows the endpoint refused (>20000 results) re-read chunk by chunk; 180 windows, all aligned to scan chunk boundaries

narrative.payments: api.imd.fun/requests/capabilities chain 1 entry: asset 0xd34a99bc..., payTo 0x4e0fa57b..., intake 0xa43e6f75..., legacy 0x1397434c...; job.open 0.5 IMD. 7384 transfers into payTo (7359 of exactly 0.5 IMD) and 15 out (sweeps); no Transfer touches an intake, since IMD moves payer->payTo directly. A row is a transfer, not proof of an order.

The original collecting relay is private and is not used as evidence
limitations: Full replay was on one public endpoint (tenderly); the second endpoint's coverage is the sampled windows (first/last chunk + 10 payment windows) plus all balances and codes.

Raw responses of the 180 replay windows are not stored (about 250 MB); each window's response sha256 and the sha256 of its canonical log lines are in replay-tenderly.json. check.py verifies the replay's recorded results and every saved raw response offline; re-running verify_chain.py re-reads them.
Balance and supply agreement does not alone prove transfer completeness; completeness rests on the full replay's per-chunk counts and digests.
